name: Marundeeswarar Temple, T. Edaiyar (Thiruvidaiyaru)
deity: Shiva as Marundeeswarar (Idaiyatrunathar), with the Goddesses Gnanambigai and Sittridai Nayaki
period: A Paadal Petra Sthalam of Nadu Nadu on the Pennai, sung by Sundarar (8th century); Chola, Pandya and Vijayanagara inscriptions
summary: On the south bank of the Pennai near Thiruvennainallur, the Lord of Thiruvidaiyaru — sung by Sundarar — is remembered as the healer beneath the marutha tree where the sage Suka was freed from his curse.

sections.history: T. Edaiyar is a village on the southern bank of the Then Pennai in Viluppuram district, on the road between Thirukkovilur and Thiruvennainallur, and it is the Thiruvidaiyaru of the Tevaram. Its temple is one of the 276 Paadal Petra Sthalams and is counted thirteenth among those of Nadu Nadu; Sundarar sang a pathigam to its Lord, preserved in the seventh Tirumurai. The stone record is unusually full for a village shrine: inscriptions name the Chola kings Rajaraja I, Kulothunga I and Rajendra III, the Pandya Maravarman Sundara Pandya, and the Vijayanagara rulers Achyuta Raya and Sadasiva Raya. The original shrine is believed to be Chola work; the masonry seen today belongs largely to the sixteenth century.
sections.architecture: The temple covers about an acre, its shrines held within concentric rectangular walls of granite and entered through a three-tiered gopuram. The Lord is enshrined as a lingam; the Goddess is worshipped in two forms, as Gnanambigai and as Sittridai Nayaki, she of the slender waist. The marutha tree is the temple's sacred tree, and the Sittridai theertham, with the river close by, serves as its holy water.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells of the sage Suka, who overheard a secret teaching that Shiva was giving to Parvati and fell under a curse for it. Shiva assured him that he would be born as the son of Vyasa, and that by worshipping the Lord at Thiruvidaiyaru he would at last be released. Suka came here and did penance beneath the marutha tree, and the curse fell away. Here devotees honour the Lord as Marundeeswarar, the Lord who is himself medicine.
sections.festivals: The temple's most prominent festival falls in the Tamil month of Thai, in January–February. Maha Shivaratri, Karthigai Deepam and Arudra Darshanam are kept as at the other Pennai-bank shrines, with the monthly pradosham; confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: Thiruvidaiyaru is a peaceful riverside village, and its walls carry six centuries of royal gifts. Pilgrims often visit it together with Thiruvennainallur, where Sundarar was claimed by the Lord, and the temples of Thirukkovilur upstream — a short circuit of Pennai shrines sung in the Tevaram.

visit.timings: Open daily in morning and evening sessions with a midday closure, as at most village temples. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left outside before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is not permitted inside the sanctum; in the outer corridors, ask the temple staff before taking pictures, especially of rituals and the festival bronzes.
visit.gettingThere: T. Edaiyar lies about 5 km from Thiruvennainallur on the road to Thirukkovilur. Villupuram, about 25 km away by road, is the nearest major railway junction; Chennai and Tiruchirappalli are the nearest major airports, with Puducherry also within reach by road.
